doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First music heard and the school band with Russo
summary: He recalls radio bands with his mother, and a school band with Bill Russo and Sy Toff; a ringing phone interrupts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What was the first music you remember hearing?

Probably you know, Glen Miller, and Harry James and some of those bands that were recording for the Chesterfield cigarettes’ fifteen-minute program. My mother and I used to listen to them. Then in the evenings, listening to different bands broadcasting from areas around the States with the covers over the radio, and my head, and things like that. So that was very inspirational for me.
Did you hear music much around Chicago?
Oh, just with the kids, in school we had a band, Russo was in high school with me, and Sy Toff and there was a high school band.
What high school did you go to?
[Konitz’s home telephone rings in the background]
Oh, lord . . . [The interview pauses for 27 seconds to let the telephone ring]
